definition: 50 genuinely distinct original article URLs opened individually and selected presentation/commentary excerpts examined. These notes do NOT represent complete reading of all author panels, original editions, 1962 missal validation, permissions or approved product content.

records.articleTitle: St Martin Iᵉʳ, pape et martyr
records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The presentation offers two rival explanations of the November 11–12 feast rearrangement between Martin of Tours, Pope Martin I and Menas; its papal burial-date witnesses also differ.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The source contrasts rival identifications of Vital: father of Gervasius/Protasius or associate of Agricola; the older April 28 memorial was suppressed in the 1960 calendar, while the Vestina church witness is older.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The introduction contrasts a pre-1955 exceptional Friday Office after Ascension octave with changed 1955/1960 lessons and Pentecost Vigil placement.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The article distinguishes Theodore of Amasea's martyrdom and eastern cult from the later November 9 dedication of his Roman church below the Palatine.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: ICRSP and Schuster distinguish Miltiades/Melchiades burial on January 10 from December 10 feast through divergent textual dating; his martyr title need not establish blood martyrdom.

records.articleTitle: Sts Basilide, Quirin, Nabor et Nazaire, Martyrs
records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The source explicitly explains that the four martyrs' collective feast aggregated three originally distinct calendars; Schuster separately discusses Quirin of Siscia's translation to Rome.

records.articleTitle: St Pierre Chrysologue, évêque, confesseur et docteur
records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The source dates Peter Chrysologus's Ravenna episcopate and later Doctor title, while Guéranger treats anti-Eutychian preaching as an Advent Incarnation theme.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: Early sacramentaries and the seventh-century lectionary witness Mark and Marcellian's Roman cult on the via Ardeatina; the detailed Sebastian-family episode is a later Passion narrative.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: Menas of Egypt had a pilgrimage shrine near Alexandria and a Roman Ostian-road titular sanctuary; pilgrim oil flasks depict two camels, with cult influencing the Martin-of-Tours feast chronology.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: Eusebius of Vercelli's ordination and death dates are distinguished from his December feast; Guéranger styles him martyr for anti-Arian sufferings without reporting execution.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The page provides Norbert's Premonstratensian order chronology while Guéranger narrates the lightning-fall conversion as a Pauline analogy.

records.articleTitle: 3ᵉ jour dans l’Octave de la Toussaint
records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The former All Saints octave was suppressed in 1955; Augustine's Sermon-on-the-Mount homilies are described as old Breviary reading, not added Mass lessons.

records.articleTitle: Sts Tiburce, Valérien et Maxime, Martyrs
records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The ancient liturgical witnesses preserve a grouped Roman cult of Tiburtius, Valerian and Maximus, while Guéranger recounts Cecilia-related family drama from their Passion.

records.articleTitle: St Grégoire le Thaumaturge, évêque et confesseur
records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The presentation dates Gregory Thaumaturgus's eastern episcopal cult; Guéranger draws a Moses–Gregory theological analogy rather than a literal biography parallel.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The Sacred Heart octave, established in 1929 and suppressed in 1955, is documented with old Matins lessons and former ranks; none constitutes a 1962 octave day.

records.articleTitle: St Urbain I, Pape et Martyr
records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The introduction itself distinguishes Pope Urban I buried at Callixtus from another Urban buried at Praetextatus, later merged through Cecilia's Passion.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The Ascension Tuesday page explicitly retains old Matins readings while acknowledging suppression of the Ascension octave in 1955; Guéranger reflects on the ascended Christ as intercessor.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: Gordian and Epimachus were remembered on the Via Latina but some early Roman sources mention only Gordian; Guéranger emphasizes their different martyrdom contexts.

records.articleTitle: 7ᵉ jour dans l’Octave de la Toussaint
records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: Former November 7 All Saints octave commentary contains Chrysostom's exhortation about Christian hope in bereavement, presented through Guéranger; exact original locus not yet collated.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The presentation links Pudenziana's Roman titular basilica to a Pudens property and distinguishes early church/site witness from the later virgin and Praxedes legend.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: Guéranger explicitly admits Barbara's local legend lacks the authority of universally promulgated Roman Breviary lessons; later artillery/lightning patronage should remain qualified.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The November 8 final All Saints octave day draws on old patristic Breviary lectures and Guéranger's hope of heaven meditation; the octave was suppressed in 1955.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: A former Sacred Heart octave article deliberately supplies Pius XII's 1956 Haurietis aquas as added editorial teaching, noting the octave ended in 1955; the encyclical is not an old rite's proper reading.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: Donatus of Arezzo's early sources give an episcopal confessor designation while a later Passio makes him martyr; ICRSP describes a change to the Mass formulary in 1920.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The source records Andrew Avellino's death while approaching the altar and historical calendar displacement of Tryphon, Respicius and Nympha; the saint's dramatic death account is hagiographic context.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: Silvester Gozzolini founded the Silvestrine order around Monte Fano; Guéranger's Benedictine-branch imagery is spiritual interpretation, not a monastic charter.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The host records Xavier's death on December 2 and Roman feast on December 3; Guéranger connects mission to Advent apostolate, with historical missionary rhetoric requiring context.

records.articleTitle: 7ᵉ jour dans l’Octave de l’Immaculée Conception
records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The old Immaculate Conception octave, removed in 1955, once included Ineffabilis Deus at Matins; Guéranger quotes a devotional Francis de Sales narration of Mary and infant John.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The Roman Via Flaminia basilica supports Valentine's cult; Guéranger acknowledges few secure biographical details, despite popular later Passio traditions.

records.articleTitle: Vendredi de la 1ʳᵉ semaine de l’Avent
records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: Guéranger reflects on Isaiah chapter 6 as a Matins-based Incarnation contrast between God's heavenly glory and the hidden birth, not an Advent Friday Mass lesson.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The Roch entry calls his votive formulary Pro aliquibus locis and makes a claim about any priest using it under 1960 rubrics; actual 1962 calendar and votive permissions require independent certification.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The article identifies Cosmas and Damian's Roman Forum basilica anniversary and embeds a September 27 1619 sermon by Francis de Sales in historic spelling.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The article asserts Hyginus instituted baptismal sponsors and church dedication rules, claims that need early historical documentary evidence; its martyrdom narrative is not independently certified.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The article distinguishes Elisabeth of Hungary's 1231 death, 1235 canonization and changing 1568/1670/1671 universal feast status.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: Romuald's translation to Fabriano (1467), his older death date and Roman feast are separate from Guéranger's account of Camaldolese Benedictine spiritual descent.

records.articleTitle: Jeudi de la 1ʳᵉ semaine de l’Avent
records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: Guéranger applies the vineyard tenants Gospel parable to Advent preparation through a prophetic meditation; not evidence of a new Thursday Mass Gospel.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: Radegund's former Frankish queenship and Poitiers Holy Cross monastery are presented alongside Guéranger's dramatic narrative of Thuringian captivity.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The former Wednesday Ascension octave includes archived Matins and Guéranger's meditation on Ascension despite acknowledging its suppression in 1955.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The old Ascension octave-day page explicitly explains the 1955 change replacing special Ephesians Office lections; historic texts may support historical Calendar notes only.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: Chrysogonus of Aquileia was honored through a Roman Trastevere titular church; Schuster notes the lack of suburban martyr burial evidence and challenges treating him as a Roman martyr.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The former Sacred Heart octave's Tuesday page substitutes Leo XIII Annum sacrum (1899) as thematic reading; it explicitly explains that Guéranger could not have commented on the 1929 octave.

records.articleTitle: les développements du Sanctoral de Grégoire XIII à Jean XXIII
records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The substantial 1960 La Maison-Dieu historical Sanctoral essay compares dates/ranks under Pius V and John XXIII and warns that ad libitum precedes obligatory observance.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The Luke entry reproduces a 1621 Francis de Sales profession sermon invoking Luke as physician and an ecclesiastical tradition of the evangelist as painter.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The 1907 calendar inclusion for Our Lady of Lourdes is followed by Guéranger's Flood-rainbow Marian analogy; the devotional parallel is not a biblical claim of historical fulfilment.

records.articleTitle: St Thomas d’Aquin, confesseur et docteur
records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: Aquinas's canonization in 1323 and Doctor title in 1567 are distinct historical acts; Guéranger emphasizes the saint's theological writings in Advent/Lent devotional context.

records.articleTitle: 5ᵉ jour dans l’Octave de la Toussaint
records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The former fifth day of All Saints octave adds a reference to a local feast of Holy Relics but explicitly identifies the 1955 octave suppression.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The Verdun local St Vanne article says his early Life was lost, then recounts the later monastery and Saint-Vanne-and-Hidulf congregation's seventeenth-century development.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The older Pudenziana page repeats the early basilica and 645 lectionary information of the newer page, and includes saintly biography drawn from late narrative traditions.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The Saint Francis of Paola article reports changes in feast rank under successive pontificates, while Guéranger discusses penitential asceticism.

records.sourceExcerptLocator: ICRSP article > Commentaires > Présentation and/or a directly read labelled commentary opening
records.sourceObservation: The Antoninus of Florence source distinguishes 1459 death from 10 May observance and traces Dominican teaching and episcopal activity through Guéranger.
